A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam.name: A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam
A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam.questStatement: The 287th Hunter Exam has begun, and only the most determined candidates will survive its brutal phases.
A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam.mainObjective: Complete all phases of the Hunter Exam and claim a Hunter License
A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam.completionCondition: Examinee passes the final exam phase, defeats or ties in the tournament bracket, and receives official Hunter License from the Association
A1-Pass the 287th Hunter Exam.questDesignBrief: The foundational quest of the entire world. Players navigate multiple exam phases: the preliminary trick tower, the island badge hunt, and the final tournament. Each phase tests combat, strategy, and character. The quest culminates in the tournament where rivals clash and secrets emerge. Tonpa's sabotage, Hisoka's unsettling presence, and the revelation of Illumi's true identity thread through encounters.

A1-The Rookie Crusher.name: A1-The Rookie Crusher
A1-The Rookie Crusher.questStatement: Tonpa, the returning 'Rookie Crusher,' targets vulnerable candidates with sabotage and psychological manipulation to ensure their failure.
A1-The Rookie Crusher.mainObjective: Survive Tonpa's machinations and expose his sabotage tactics
A1-The Rookie Crusher.completionCondition: Player defeats Tonpa in combat or disables his sabotage network by helping fellow examinees recognize his schemes; Tonpa is disqualified or withdraws
A1-The Rookie Crusher.questDesignBrief: A side-thread examining the social dynamics of the exam. Tonpa is a recurring antagonist who uses poisoned tea, theft, and rumor-spreading to undermine newcomers. His motivations are cowardly and petty—he sees the Exam as his domain and newcomers as threats. Players encounter his victims and can either help them directly or orchestrate his public humiliation. This quest explores how bullying operates within the competitive Hunter framework.

A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate.name: A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate
A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate.questStatement: Killua has been taken home by his family after disqualification. Reaching the legendary Zoldyck Estate requires passing the Testing Gate and winning over a family of world-famous assassins.
A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate.mainObjective: Reach Killua at Kukuroo Mountain and convince the Zoldyck family to release him
A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate.completionCondition: Party reaches the interior of the Zoldyck Estate, confronts Silva and Kikyo, and Killua is released via Silva's bargain or proven worthiness
A2-Reach the Zoldyck Estate.questDesignBrief: The rescue quest. Players begin at the Testing Gate with doors weighing progressively more (1st door: 4 tons). They must either train until they can open doors legitimately or find alternate paths (butlers' shortcuts, influence trades). Encounters with Gotoh, Canary, and other butlers reveal the family's strict code and Killua's internal conflict. The climax involves Silva offering a bargain: Killua may leave if he swears to return when his adventure is complete. This quest establishes the Zoldycks as a force in the world and Killua's deep family psychology.

A2-The Butler's Dilemma.name: A2-The Butler's Dilemma
A2-The Butler's Dilemma.questStatement: Canary, a young Zoldyck butler, faces a crisis of loyalty when Gon and friends arrive—her duty to the family wars with her sympathy for Killua's desire for freedom.
A2-The Butler's Dilemma.mainObjective: Navigate Canary's loyalty conflict and help her choose her own path
A2-The Butler's Dilemma.completionCondition: Canary either reaffirms her loyalty to the family or chooses independence; outcome depends on player choices throughout the arc
A2-The Butler's Dilemma.questDesignBrief: An intimate character study of one of the Estate's youngest staff. Canary is bound by training but not hardened like the butlers or family members. Players encounter her multiple times—she may aid them secretly, confront them directly, or wrestle with her conscience. Her ultimate choice reflects the players' moral approach to the Estate. This side quest adds emotional depth by showing that even the Zoldyck system has fracture points.

A3-Climb to the 200th Floor.name: A3-Climb to the 200th Floor
A3-Climb to the 200th Floor.questStatement: Heavens Arena beckons with wealth and glory—but the 200th floor marks a deadly threshold where Nen ability separates the worthy from the doomed.
A3-Climb to the 200th Floor.mainObjective: Ascend through Heavens Arena and claim ten consecutive victories beyond the 200th floor
A3-Climb to the 200th Floor.completionCondition: Player reaches floor 200+, survives Nen baptism encounter with a floor master, earns ten wins with dignity and honor
A3-Climb to the 200th Floor.questDesignBrief: The training quest. Players enter Heavens Arena as novices and climb through tournament brackets against increasingly skilled fighters. Lower floors introduce combat basics and arena culture. Floor 200 is the Nen initiation—an encounter with a master that reveals Nen exists (prior arcs conceal this). Hisoka serves as a floor 200 gatekeeper and potential mentor. Wing appears as the true teacher, offering honest Nen instruction. Victories must be earned through skill growth, not mere luck. This quest transforms players from unawakened to Nen-aware practitioners.

A3-The Teacher's Stake.name: A3-The Teacher's Stake
A3-The Teacher's Stake.questStatement: Wing and his student Zushi guard the truth of authentic Nen teaching—a secret philosophy at odds with the underground fighting culture's brutal surface magic.
A3-The Teacher's Stake.mainObjective: Learn the true principles of Nen from Wing and prove yourself as a worthy student
A3-The Teacher's Stake.completionCondition: Player completes Wing's full curriculum: Ten, Ren, Hatsu mastery, and Water Divination; defeats Zushi in controlled sparring or passes Wing's final test of character
A3-The Teacher's Stake.questDesignBrief: A meditation on mentorship. Wing is rare—an honest teacher in a world of manipulation. His stakes are philosophical: he demands students approach Nen with respect and discipline, not hunger for power. Players who align with his values gain access to his deepest teachings; those who view Nen as mere weapon find him aloof. Zushi serves as a peer challenger and reflection of Wing's teaching philosophy. This quest is optional but rewards alignment with authentic mastery over shortcuts.

A4-Auction Season.name: A4-Auction Season
A4-Auction Season.questStatement: Yorknew City's underground auction draws the world's most dangerous players—mafia, hunters, thieves, and worse. The Phantom Troupe's massacre will reshape the event and everyone in it.
A4-Auction Season.mainObjective: Navigate the auction season, survive the Troupe's assault, and choose your faction's response
A4-Auction Season.completionCondition: Player completes auction-related objectives (acquire target items, defend clients, or execute faction goals), navigates the Troupe massacre, and reaches a safe conclusion
A4-Auction Season.questDesignBrief: The political quest. Players may serve multiple roles: Zoldyck assassins hired for Ten Don protection, Hunters investigating black market crime, or mafia retainers securing goods. The Phantom Troupe's massacre happens mid-arc as a story event, forcing improvisation. Kurapika's vendetta thread weaves through; the chain sealing of Chrollo reshapes power dynamics. This quest teaches that Hunters are not heroes—they are tools wielded by powers above them, and moral choices are rarely clear.

A4-The Scarlet Market.name: A4-The Scarlet Market
A4-The Scarlet Market.questStatement: Kurta clan Scarlet Eyes circulate through Yorknew's black market like currency of grief—a hunter's treasure hunt that doubles as genocide remembrance.
A4-The Scarlet Market.mainObjective: Locate and trace a pair of Scarlet Eyes through the underground market network
A4-The Scarlet Market.completionCondition: Player identifies Scarlet Eye dealers, maps their supply network, and either acquires the eyes or brings them to Kurapika; optionally: helps Kurapika pursue a Troupe member
A4-The Scarlet Market.questDesignBrief: An investigation quest tied to the Kurta massacre. Scarlet Eyes are priceless artifacts—preserved in glass vials, hoarded by collectors, traded like art. Players who accept this quest become entangled in black market intrigue. They meet dealers, collectors, and Kurapika himself, learning the scope of the Troupe's crime. The quest offers moral complexity: the eyes represent both crime evidence and sacred relics. Finding them means supporting Kurapika's vengeance—a sympathetic but potentially bloody path.

A5-Clear Greed Island.name: A5-Clear Greed Island
A5-Clear Greed Island.questStatement: Greed Island is a legendary Nen-construct game hidden in the real world, offering vast wealth and rare Nen artifacts to those who gather its restricted cards.
A5-Clear Greed Island.mainObjective: Enter Greed Island and gather the required restricted cards to clear the game
A5-Clear Greed Island.completionCondition: Player enters the game, collects all designated restricted cards, defeats the Bomber trio or negotiates a cease-fire, and emerges victorious
A5-Clear Greed Island.questDesignBrief: The training gauntlet. Greed Island is a curated challenge by Ging and other masters—players enter via ring and immediately face card-gathering tasks. The Bomber trio is the primary obstacle, farming players via Countdown bombs. Biscuit Krueger appears as a recruiter and secret powerhouse trainer. The game teaches Nen mastery through necessity: players gain spell cards, learn combat through alliance politics, and ultimately access resources that advance their capabilities. This quest is the longest single arc and culminates in meeting Kite, who bridges to the Chimera Ant crisis.

A5-The Dodgeball King.name: A5-The Dodgeball King
A5-The Dodgeball King.questStatement: Razor, Greed Island's game master and a legendary Nen prodigy, offers a final challenge: defeat his 14 Nen-beast devils at their own game.
A5-The Dodgeball King.mainObjective: Defeat Razor's 14 Nen-beast devils in a dodgeball match and earn Razor's respect
A5-The Dodgeball King.completionCondition: Party defeats the devils through strategy, teamwork, and Nen mastery; Razor acknowledges their victory and grants passage or rewards
A5-The Dodgeball King.questDesignBrief: An optional but rewarding trial. Razor is a cheerful powerhouse who teaches through sport. His devils are Nen constructs born from his aura, each with distinct personalities and abilities. Defeating them requires genuine teamwork and creative Nen application. Hisoka may ally with players here, revealing his Bungee Gum properties in combat. Victory grants immense respect and potential alliance, while defeat is humbling but teaches valuable lessons. This quest rewards ingenuity and friendship over raw power.

A6-The NGL Incursion.name: A6-The NGL Incursion
A6-The NGL Incursion.questStatement: A Chimera Ant outbreak in the isolated nation of NGL spreads human-insect hybrid soldiers across the continent. The investigation may become an invasion.
A6-The NGL Incursion.mainObjective: Investigate the Chimera Ant outbreak from the NGL border through the palace invasion
A6-The NGL Incursion.completionCondition: Player investigates nest origins, fights ant squads, participates in the palace invasion, and contributes to Meruem's defeat or negotiation
A6-The NGL Incursion.questDesignBrief: The apocalypse quest. This arc contains the campaign's highest stakes and darkest content. Kite's death early on sets the tone—heroes die here. The Royal Guards and Meruem are Master-tier mythic NPCs whose power redefines the campaign baseline. The palace invasion is a coalition effort requiring political navigation. Players may befriend ants-who-remember-being-human, fight alongside Netero, or pursue personal vendettas. Gon's catastrophic transformation (spending his Nen permanently) is the arc's emotional climax. This quest teaches that victory demands sacrifice.

A6-Hearts of the Colony.name: A6-Hearts of the Colony
A6-Hearts of the Colony.questStatement: Some Chimera Ants retain memories of humanity—Colt, Ikalgo, Meleoron—and face impossible choices between loyalty to the colony and loyalty to their former lives.
A6-Hearts of the Colony.mainObjective: Navigate the paths of Chimera Ants caught between two worlds and shape their fates
A6-Hearts of the Colony.completionCondition: Player encounters at least three human-memory ants, learns their stories, and influences whether they survive, defect, or sacrifice themselves
A6-Hearts of the Colony.questDesignBrief: An intimacy quest within the apocalypse. Colt is a squadron leader bound to the King by vow; Ikalgo struggles with his dual nature; Meleoron is a soldier who befriends Knuckle. These NPCs are living bridges between species. Players who engage with them gain allies, information, and moral complexity—these ants are not monsters; they are people. The quest rewards empathy without erasing tragedy. Some ants may ally with players; others must be fought. This side quest maintains the arc's thematic depth: not everyone is purely good or evil.

A7-The 13th Chairman Election.name: A7-The 13th Chairman Election
A7-The 13th Chairman Election.questStatement: Netero's death triggers an election circus among the Zodiacs—twelve of the world's most powerful hunters vie for the Chairman seat through political intrigue and hidden agendas.
A7-The 13th Chairman Election.mainObjective: Navigate the election politics, survive Pariston's games, and determine the new leadership
A7-The 13th Chairman Election.completionCondition: Player participates in multiple election rounds, survives Pariston's machinations, witnesses Leorio's symbolic punch, and sees a new Chairman elected
A7-The 13th Chairman Election.questDesignBrief: The political endgame. The Zodiacs emerge from shadow—powerful, quirky, and self-interested. Pariston is a magnificent bastard orchestrating chaos for amusement. Ging appears as Zodiac Boar and Gon's father, a reunion filtered through confusion and anger. Kurapika and Leorio join as new Zodiacs, marking their rise. The quest teaches that institutional power is often comedy and farce. Pariston's games serve no purpose except his own enjoyment. The election is won through charisma, alliances, and spectacle, not merit. This quest is primarily political rather than combat-focused.

A7-A Wish for a Life.name: A7-A Wish for a Life
A7-A Wish for a Life.questStatement: Gon lies comatose, his Nen spent in a vow that nearly killed him. Killua races to find Alluka, the legendary wish-granter hidden in his family vault, before it is too late.
A7-A Wish for a Life.mainObjective: Help Killua locate and retrieve Alluka, then navigate her wish-granting rules to save Gon
A7-A Wish for a Life.completionCondition: Party finds Alluka, Killua successfully negotiates Nanika's requirements, and Alluka's power heals Gon (at escalating cost)
A7-A Wish for a Life.questDesignBrief: A race against time and family. Killua is desperate—Gon is dying and only Alluka's impossible wish-granting power can save him. But Alluka is locked away by the Zoldyck family, and Illumi hunts Killua to control Alluka for his own purposes. The quest involves escaping Illumi's pursuit, deceiving or defeating the family, and managing Nanika's escalating wishes (which may require terrible prices: trading lifespan, physical transformation, or moral compromises). This quest is intimate—about friendship's limits and what Killua will sacrifice. It also introduces Nanika as a mystery: she is not explained even in canon. Players encounter her alien logic and otherworldly power without full understanding.

A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale.name: A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale
A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale.questStatement: The Black Whale, a 200,000-passenger expedition ship, sails toward the Dark Continent—but the Succession War within rages as deadly as any external threat.
A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale.mainObjective: Survive the Black Whale crossing and navigate the Succession War's chaos, wards, and alliances
A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale.completionCondition: Player reaches the Dark Continent shore, survives Nen-beast encounters, avoids assassination from rival princes, and completes personal arcs
A8-The Voyage of the Black Whale.questDesignBrief: The open-ended sandbox. The Black Whale is a floating nation with 14 princes, their soldiers, the Zodiacs, the Phantom Troupe hunting Hisoka, and Kurapika guarding young Woble. Every faction has goals; alliances shift constantly. Nen beasts—parasitic vow-guardians tied to each prince—are incomprehensible threats that defy tier. This quest offers maximum player agency: form alliances, pursue vendettas, or focus on survival. Outcomes of the Succession War are extrapolated (manga incomplete). This quest teaches that the world persists beyond players' control—they influence events, not determine them. The Dark Continent itself remains largely mysterious.

A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen.name: A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen
A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen.questStatement: Queen Oito and her young son Woble face the Succession War's brutality with no power of their own—bodyguards are their only defense against assassination.
A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen.mainObjective: Protect Oito and Woble through the Succession War without permanent political entanglement
A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen.completionCondition: Player keeps Woble alive through multiple assassination attempts, learns court intrigue secrets, and reaches the Dark Continent with Oito's faction intact
A8-Bodyguard to the Forgotten Queen.questDesignBrief: A protective escort quest with political teeth. Woble is nearly powerless—a young prince with no Nen beast (yet) and no faction of consequence. Oito is his mother, intelligent but isolated. Players hired as bodyguards must navigate other princes' assassination attempts, the Zodiacs' schemes, Tserriednich's terrifying Specialist powers, and the boat's paranoia. The quest offers protection challenges without direct combat solutions (assassination is subtle). Outcomes are EXTRAPOLATED per arc spec—manga ends before this subplot concludes. Success is measured by keeping both alive and maintaining some dignity and autonomy for the Queen.
